summary.value: The Golden Comet is a sex-linked hybrid layer, not a true breed, first produced by the Hubbard hatchery in the United States. It comes from mating a New Hampshire Red rooster with a White Rock or Rhode Island White hen, and chicks can be sexed by color at hatch. It is sold under many names, including Red Star, Golden Buff and Cinnamon Queen. Hens are reddish brown to gold, with a single red comb and yellow, clean legs. They can start laying at about 16 weeks and give roughly 260 to 330 brown eggs a year, but output drops after about two years, and they rarely go broody. Golden Comets are calm, friendly and easy to handle. They manage both cold and hot weather if given shade and water, though the comb can frostbite. They suit beginners who mainly want eggs.
